answer: Special Ops shadow rule: watch when identities go dark together. Every agent answers a tiny signed heartbeat at random minutes, and the ledger keeps a months-long atlas of who blinked out when. Real machines fail on their own schedules; a farm shares one power strip, one ferrous rack, one API quota, so its clones drop and return in the same seconds. Identities whose outages overlap far beyond chance merge into one share. Faking independence means separate hosts, networks and providers per name, not a nebula of clones that flickers at once.
